readout_other: von Frey; hot plate; sciatic CMAP electromyography; DRG patch-clamp; RNA-seq; ELISA; immunofluorescence
direction_notes: LIFU to the injured sciatic nerve raised mechanical and thermal pain thresholds in CCI rats, reduced CMAP amplitude (nerve excitability) and suppressed inward sodium currents in cultured DRG neurons.
safety_notes: Skin burns were observed in early experiments when the irradiation duration was prolonged; no additional damage to deeper tissues was detected beyond the original injury.

exposures.label: LIFU to CCI sciatic nerve (transcutaneous) and exposed nerve for EMG

timing.protocol_description: Transcutaneous stimulation for 3 min at 0.5 Hz PRF, 5% duty cycle (Figure 1 legend states 4 min); for EMG the exposed nerve was irradiated for 1 min with the same parameters. Frequency of treatment sessions not stated.
Cultured neurons exposed for 30 s at 1 Hz PRF, 20% duty cycle; recorded immediately or after 1 h or 2 h incubation.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Results: Compared with the CCI group, rats in the CCI + LIFU group showed significantly increased mechanical and thermal pain thresholds (n = 7, P < 0.05), with no difference between Sham and Normal groups.
